titulo: Family and possessives: Describing your family and how many you are

aula.objetivo: Name family members in the masculine and feminine, form the mixed plural («los hermanos»), use the possessives «mi, tu, su, nuestro, vuestro» with the right agreement, show possession with «de», and say how many people are in your household.

sessao.titulo: Describing your family and how many you are

blocos.titulo: De for possession, mayor and menor, somos…
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to say who something belongs to, Spanish uses «de» + the owner, not an apostrophe-s: «el libro de Ana», «la casa de mis abuelos». With the article, «de + el» becomes «del»: «el coche del profesor». STEP 2: «mayor» means the older one (of two siblings, or in a group): «mi hermano mayor». «Menor» means the younger one: «mi hermana menor». Many speakers also say «pequeño, pequeña». STEP 3: «mayor» can also mean an older person, as in elderly: «mis abuelos son mayores». STEP 4: to count how many people make up the family, use «ser»: «Somos cuatro en mi familia.» Or «tener»: «Tengo una familia pequeña». STEP 5: for marital status, the common usage is «ser soltero / soltera» and «estar casado / casada» (the contrast between «ser» and «estar» comes in lesson 10): «Soy soltera», «Mis padres están casados». STEP 6: when introducing someone, use «Este es…» or «Esta es…» and then the possessive: «Esta es mi hermana, Elena». STEP 7: last names: traditionally the first one is the father's and the second one is the mother's. «Mi apellido es García López» means the father is a García and the mother a López. In Spain, on marrying, each person keeps their own last names. STEP 8: when speaking respectfully about an older person, say «don Manuel» or «doña Rosa» before their first name (not their last name).
blocos.comparacao: English also uses «of» plus an apostrophe-s for possession, and the key difference is the mandatory contraction: «del» (de + el), and no article before a person's name. Watch out for «mayor»: in a family context it means «older», not «larger» in size (which is «más grande»).

erros.errado: [misto] Es el coche de el profesor.

erros.motivo: «Mayor» means the older one; «maior» doesn't exist in Spanish.

erros.errado: [misto] Somos cuatro personas en la familia.

blocos.titulo: Una foto de familia / A family photo
blocos.contexto: Marta shows Javier a family photo.

linhas.ru: — Mira, Javier, esta es mi familia.
linhas.pt: — Look, Javier, this is my family.
linhas.audio: Mira, Javier, esta es mi familia.

linhas.ru: — Son mis padres, Rosa y Manuel, y mis abuelos.
linhas.pt: — They're my parents, Rosa and Manuel, and my grandparents.
linhas.audio: Son mis padres, Rosa y Manuel, y mis abuelos.

linhas.ru: — Sí, tengo un hermano mayor y una hermana menor.
linhas.pt: — Yes, I have an older brother and a younger sister.
linhas.audio: Sí, tengo un hermano mayor y una hermana menor.

linhas.pt: — So there are five of you at home.

linhas.ru: — No, somos seis, con mi abuela.
linhas.pt: — No, there are six of us, with my grandmother.
linhas.audio: No, somos seis, con mi abuela.

blocos.enunciado: Write and say five sentences about someone in your family: name, age, where they live, with «mayor» or «menor», and one sentence with «de».
Give the possessive for each person (yo, tú, él, nosotros, vosotros, ellos) with a family word.
